title: Disruption by Andrew Stein at the Pershing Square Signature Center #d...
transcript: I find that almost all AI-focused plays are saying the same thing, but at least some of them are fairly realistic or dramatically interesting. This one kinda misses the mark on both spectrums, despite boasting an impressive ensemble cast and a sleek, appropriately futuristic production design. John David Washington plays a hotshot entrepreneur who's trying to get his old college buddies to invest in his new AI endeavor, much to the dismay of their wives. At the same time, all of these couples are going through their own issues, which not so coincidentally makes them the perfect candidates to use this new technology. I was underwhelmed by how predictable this play was, but I was more disappointed by its immense amount of exposition over progression. Because the plot itself requires a lot of direct explanation, with it being largely about a fictional, cutting edge technology, it felt especially cumbersome. It wasn't a complete wash, though — the cast did surprisingly well with their underdeveloped characters, and the scene work was natural and humorous, despite the artificial nature of the story. If you wanna see a great cast, by all means, see this play. If you wanna be spooked about AI, just read the news. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer found the play predictable and exposition-heavy, saying it missed the mark dramatically. Praise is limited to cast and design, with a lukewarm 'if you want a great cast' recommendation that leans negative overall.
